scenes.captionEN: Mama set down the porridge. Four bowls, four spoons—and warm bread in the middle.
“This piece?” asked Papa. PinPin held out both paws. “That piece!”
PomPom tapped his spoon. Mama tapped hers back. Tap, tap!
PinPin carried his empty bowl to Mama. “Now can we play?”

requests.evidence: Contact inspected: table bowls and bread, Papa-to-child bread handoff, Mama/baby spoons, then empty-bowl clearing. This is a four-beat eating sequence; not merely breakfast preparation.

scenes.captionEN: PinPin picked up one little bucket. “I'll be quick!”
Out through the front door went PinPin and Rabbit. The empty bucket bumped gently against his knee.
“The spring is this way,” said Rabbit. PinPin followed with his bucket.
“Water first, then our boats,” said PinPin. Rabbit held up the two leaves.
The spring splashed over the stones. “Hello, PinPin!” chirped two little birds.
PinPin held his bucket under the stream. Glug, glug, glug.
The little bird shook its wet feathers all around PinPin. “My bath has started!”
Rabbit set their leaf boats afloat. One went straight; the other went round and round!
“See you later!” called PinPin. He picked up his full bucket and started home.
“One bucket, Mama!” Mama held the door open. “The bath is waiting.”
PinPin carried the bucket carefully. A little splash landed on his toes.
He poured his bucket into the bath. The bottom was only just covered.
PinPin looked at his bucket, then at the big bath. “That will take lots of trips.”
“I could finish the bath before our next game,” thought PinPin. “I could make the water come here!”

requests.request: Reveal Beaver and Bear working; greet, participate, fabricate aqueduct

scenes.captionEN: Tap, tap, tap. PinPin listened. “Someone is building something!”
Between the trees, Beaver and Mr. Bear were making a little wooden walkway. A blue tractor stood beside the planks.
“Good morning!” said Mr. Bear. He put down his plank and waved one enormous paw.
“This way, paws stay out of the mud,” Beaver explained. PinPin tried one dry step.
scenes.reportedReview: agent visual pass; root review pending

scenes.captionEN: Mr. Bear held the next board. PinPin passed Beaver a little wooden peg.
Over bread and fruit, PinPin told Beaver about the bath. “It keeps filling, even when nobody is splashing!”
Beaver drew a little path in the earth. “We’ll give the water a road of its own.”
He joined two little wooden gutters. “This end goes a little lower.”
PinPin tipped the little jug. The water ran down, from one piece into the next.
Beaver shaped the wood. Papa checked the edges, and PinPin stacked the little supports.
“Long pieces coming through!” Mr. Bear carried them easily. Papa showed him the clear space.

requests.request: At least five actual homeward travel/arrival images

scenes.captionEN: “Wait.” Scooby waited. Papa checked both bundles. PinPin checked that his toes had room.
“Thank you!” called PinPin. Mr. Bear lifted a paw, and Beaver waved his little plane.
The leaves brushed softly above them. Scooby carried his passengers and the little wooden road.
“Low branch!” said Papa. Two hedgehog heads dipped together.
Clack, clack went the wooden pieces. PinPin tapped the same rhythm on Papa's paw.
“There's our roof!” PinPin pointed between the trees. Scooby's ears turned forward.
Mama heard Scooby on the path. She opened the door before PinPin could knock.

requests.evidence: First two are load check and farewell; exactly five intended homeward beats are 32i3–32i7: ride, duck branch, rhythm, spot roof, arrival. All seven unselected at audit snapshot. Do not count packing/farewell as the five travel shots.

requests.request: Aqueduct persists from installation through authorized disassembly

scenes.captionEN: They laid one end over the next. PinPin held it while Papa joined the pieces.
Papa moved the little blocks underneath. Each piece rested a little lower.
The water ran along their wooden path. It passed the table without wetting the legs.
Papa stepped over the gutter with breakfast. PinPin brought the spoons.
Papa passed the warm toast. PinPin took a big, happy bite.
Mama shared the sweet berries. PomPom opened his little mouth for another spoonful.
“I'll gather the flowers out of the bath,” said PinPin. “Then I can see the water.”
A leaf covered the doorway. “Excuse me,” said Mama.
Mama bent lower. The leaf had become a green ceiling.
Papa put both paws on the pot. “A little push!”
Papa and PinPin carried the pot. Mama held PomPom and showed them the clear doorway.
PinPin jumped. His paw went right past it.
Mama opened the window. “This way!”
They waved a towel together. The bubbles sailed outside.
The bubbles were gone. PinPin watched the little stream in the bath.
Mama crouched beside him. “What are you thinking?”
Papa lifted the gutters away. PinPin carried the little blocks.
